name: Carlos Huaman
bio:
Carlos Huaman's journey into motorsport started in his small village nestled in the Andes, where he spent his youth tinkering with old trucks and motorcycles. He quickly developed a knack for understanding how things worked, eventually leading him to an apprenticeship at a local machine shop. Eager to expand his horizons, Carlos moved to Lima, where he secured a position with a racing team, initially handling basic repairs and maintenance.

His meticulous approach and unwavering dedication earned him a reputation for reliability and precision. He is now a core member of Rexal FMI Racing, where he specializes in chassis fabrication and metalwork. Carlos is known for his ability to find creative solutions to complex problems, often drawing upon his deep understanding of materials and mechanics. His pragmatic mindset ensures that every component he works on meets the highest standards of performance and durability, contributing to the team's competitive edge.

What truly sets Carlos apart is his quiet determination and his commitment to continuous improvement. He's always eager to learn new techniques and technologies, ensuring that his skills remain at the forefront of motorsport engineering. His colleagues respect his work ethic and his willingness to share his expertise, making him a valuable asset to the team.

physical.description: Carlos is a man of medium build with calloused hands that speak of years spent shaping metal.

quirks: Always sharpens his tools to an obsessive degree before starting any task.
Has a specific playlist of traditional Peruvian music he listens to while working.
Meticulously cleans his workspace at the end of each day, ensuring everything is perfectly organized.
